metaDescription: Four label printers that print wide 24mm (1 inch) tape compared on connectivity, industrial features, app dependence and tape supply for shops and workshops.
expertTake: The Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT is the pick for most buyers: it prints TZe tape up to 24mm, connects by Bluetooth and USB, and stores 90 labels for repeat jobs. The PT-P710BT Cube Plus is the value pick for a phone-driven desk. If you label cables, heat-shrink tubing or panels all day, buy the PT-E510BP contractor kit instead of any office model.
introParagraphs: One inch tape is the size where a label starts to work as a sign. It carries two or three lines of readable text, wraps around thick cables and bins, and sticks to shelves and equipment that a narrow label would barely cover. Check the maximum tape width on the manufacturer's page before you buy.

This guide explains which label printers actually take this width, how tape type separates office from industrial use, and what to check about apps and tape supply. There are only a handful of true one inch machines, so this is a short list built on facts, not filler. Use the picks above as your shortlist, then read the reviews to match one to your trade.

products.name: Brother P-Touch PT-D610BT Business Professional Label Maker
products.description:
The PT-D610BT is the best all-round one inch machine because it joins a keyboard, a color-free display, Bluetooth, USB and a label memory in one body. It prints Brother TZe tape up to 24mm, a laminated tape sold in many colors and widths, and its library of 17 fonts, 160 frames and 900 symbols is the richest in this guide.

Connectivity is the practical edge. USB works for a desktop, Bluetooth for a phone, and the built-in memory stores up to 90 labels for quick reprinting. That combination suits a small shop where several people print the same labels all week. Compared with the Cube Plus, the D610BT has its own keyboard, so you can print without a phone.

The automatic cutter keeps edges square, and the tape ecosystem is wide, with compatible 24mm cassettes available from many makers. Keep a spare cassette of each tape you use, clean the print head with a swab and isopropyl alcohol when streaks appear, and update the desktop software after operating system changes. A sensible setup is to keep one cassette of clear laminated tape and one of white in the drawer, since those two cover bins, cables and shelves. Run a test label on the real surface before printing a batch, because rough or dusty surfaces need a firmer press to bond.
products.bestFor: A small business or workshop that shares one printer and labels the same things repeatedly.
pros: Prints up to 24mm laminated TZe tape
cons: Higher price than the Cube Plus

products.name: Brother P-Touch Cube Plus PT-P710BT Bluetooth Label Maker
products.description:
The Cube Plus is a small, light printer that has no keyboard at all: you design on a phone or PC and print over Bluetooth. The listing says you can choose from three different Brother software applications and pick pre-designed templates for home and home office use. It prints on TZe tape up to 24mm wide.

Because there is no keyboard, the printer itself is compact and the tape cassette is the main body weight. The tradeoff is dependence: if your phone or the app is unavailable, you cannot print. That fits a desk where a computer is always nearby but is a poor fit for a toolbox. Against the D610BT, the P710BT is cheaper and smaller but has no built-in memory.

Use it with a computer for batch jobs, since a PC application handles lists and templates faster than a phone. Keep the app updated and a spare cassette on hand. Keep the app and the printer firmware in step, and pair the printer once with a primary phone and once with the desk computer so a lost phone does not stop work. Print a short test label after every app update, since interface changes sometimes shift margins.
products.bestFor: A desk with a computer or phone nearby, where a keyboard is unnecessary.
cons: No keyboard, so it needs a phone or computer

products.name: Brother PT-E510BP Contractor Kit Handheld Industrial Label Printer

specList.label: Media
specList.value: Laminated labels and heat shrink tube

products.description:
The PT-E510BP contractor kit is an industrial handheld sold with five tapes, a carrying case and a rechargeable battery. It prints laminated labels and heat shrink tubes from 3.5mm to 24mm, and the dual auto-cutter handles both full cuts and the half cuts that make peel-off labels easy. A USB-C port connects it to a computer for data-driven jobs.

This is the machine for people who label cable, patch panels and equipment on site. Industrial tapes are built for heat, chemicals and rough handling, and a heat shrink sleeve slides over a cable end and shrinks to a permanent marker. Compared with the D610BT, the E510BP gives up the desk comfort for ruggedness and the contractor bundle.

Plan for industrial tape costs, which are higher per label than office tape. Keep spare batteries in the case, and clean the cutter blade now and then to avoid ragged edges. Charge the battery before each site visit and carry the spare tape in the case, since a dead cartridge halfway through a rack is a real waste of time. Practice the half-cut setting on scrap tape so you can peel labels cleanly with gloves on.
products.bestFor: Electricians and network installers who label cables, panels and equipment on site.
pros: Contractor kit with five tapes and a case
cons: Overkill and costly for home use
Industrial tapes cost more per label

products.name: SUPVAN T50M Pro Bluetooth Label Maker with 3 Tapes
products.description:
SUPVAN's T50M Pro prints a different class of label: wide labels from three quarters of an inch up to two inches, which brackets the 24mm size and extends well past it. The listing highlights waterproof labels, an app with more than 30 fonts and image editing from a phone, tablet or PC, and a bundle with three tapes.

Wide labels suit storage bins, food containers and shipping stickers, where a one inch strip would look thin. The tradeoff is the proprietary tape: SUPVAN's rolls are not standard TZe cassettes, so you depend on one supplier. Against the Brother models, the T50M Pro offers a bigger canvas but a narrower tape ecosystem.

If you label bins and jars rather than cables, the wider format may serve you better than a 24mm strip. Check the tape price before you commit, and keep spare rolls. Because the tape width is wider than a standard label, check the minimum order of rolls and the shipping time before you depend on it. Test a small roll on glass and plastic bins to see whether the adhesive holds in damp rooms.
products.bestFor: Storage bins, jars and containers where a wider label reads better than a strip.
pros: Prints from 3/4 to 2 inch wide labels
App with 30+ fonts and image editing

buyingCriteria.explanation: Only a few current machines print one inch tape. The Brother PT-D610BT, PT-P710BT and PT-E510BP take TZe tape up to 24mm, and the SUPVAN T50M Pro prints wider labels from 3/4 to 2 inches. Check the maximum width on the spec sheet, because many label makers stop at 12 or 18mm. For labels viewed at arm's length, 24mm tape allows text around 9 to 12 mm tall, which is easy to read without glasses. Narrower tape needs a smaller font and is harder to read across a workshop. Choose the width for the viewing distance, not for the habit of using a smaller label.

TZe laminated tape on the D610BT and P710BT survives water, sun and abrasion for indoor and outdoor labels. The PT-E510BP prints industrial tapes and heat shrink tubing for cable work. Choose industrial only if you label wires, panels or equipment. Heat shrink tube is a specialist item, and only the industrial model prints it. If you do not wire equipment, ignore that feature and put the money into tape supply instead.

The D610BT has a keyboard, so it prints without a phone. The P710BT and SUPVAN need an app or a computer. If the app is dropped or breaks, those models lose their interface. A keyboard saves time when you label items one at a time, and an app saves time when you label from a list. Decide which workflow you will actually use.

Brother TZe is sold by many makers, so compatible 24mm cassettes keep running costs down. The SUPVAN uses its own rolls, which ties you to one supplier. Compatible cassettes can halve the running cost, but test a short roll before buying a box, because adhesive quality varies by supplier.

The D610BT stores 90 labels and the E510BP supports databases from a computer. Repeat jobs, such as asset tags, are far faster with memory or import. If you print the same fifty labels every quarter, memory or database import turns an hour of typing into minutes.

A 24mm cassette costs more than a 12mm one because it holds more material, so the cost per label rises with width. Over a year a busy shop may spend more on tape than on the printer. Compatible cassettes from reputable makers lower that bill, and the Brother models can use them. SUPVAN rolls come from one source, so price changes land directly on you.

faq.q: Why are there so few 24mm label printers?
faq.a: Most home label makers stop at 12 or 18mm. One inch tape needs a wider print head, so it appears mainly on business and industrial models. Check the maximum width on the spec sheet. A common choice is 24mm for shelves and 12mm for small items, so owning one printer that takes both widths is convenient.

faq.q: Can a 24mm printer use narrower tape?
faq.a: Yes, a Brother printer that takes 24mm also takes narrower TZe tapes. Print height scales with the tape. That gives you flexibility. Printing at a larger font on narrow tape fills the label height, so the usable text size depends on the tape you load.

faq.q: Do I need an industrial model?
faq.a: Only for cable, panel or equipment labeling. Office models cover shelves, files and bins. Industrial models use tapes for heat and chemicals. Always check the maximum tape width on the manufacturer's specification page, not only on the shopping listing.

faq.q: Can I print two lines on 24mm tape?
faq.a: Yes, comfortably. On one inch tape two lines of about 7 to 9 mm text fit with a margin, and three lines fit at a smaller size. That is why this width works for shelf and bin labels that carry a name and a code. Check the printer preview to see the layout before you print.

On TZe models, compatible cassettes work, but cheap tape can jam or fade. Buy from a reputable maker. SUPVAN uses its own rolls. Test the adhesive on the real surface first, since textured plastic and powder-coated metal behave differently.

faq.q: How do I choose between laminated and non-laminated tape?
faq.a: Laminated tape, such as Brother TZe, seals the print between films and survives water, sun and abrasion. Non-laminated tape is cheaper but scuffs and fades sooner. Use laminated for garages, kitchens and outdoors, and non-laminated only for indoor files that never get wet.
